process.near_margin.measured_on: decided, not measured: how far round a part the gate looks for bought, hardware and mesh bodies before it says that a standing question cannot apply
process.near_margin.description: a body whose bounding box is farther than this from the bounding box of a part is not near that part

process.bought_hint_faces.measured_on: decided, not measured: a plain cylinder has 3 faces and a washer or a tube has 4
process.bought_hint_faces.description: a part with at most this many faces is named by `gate.py scan` as possibly bought: a hint, it changes no verdict

rules.title: No concept geometry is exported
rules.statement: No functional shape of the part is an approximation: tooth forms, cams, seats and snap fits are final, and no bought part beside it is a box or a disc. A concept says it is one, lists what is not designed yet, and is never exported as printable.
rules.why: A tooth groove that was only sketched went to print as if it were final: three pulleys were printed again.

attest.question: Is any functional shape of this part simplified, guessed or concept geometry?
labels: none: every functional shape is final
yes: listed in the report for the owner

rules.title: The changed zone was looked at
rules.statement: Every geometry edit leaves a close-up screenshot of the changed zone, and it is looked at: gaps, misaligned faces, clipped holes.
rules.why: Dents, steps and clipped holes were visible at a glance and were found by the owner in the slicer.

attest.question: Screenshot of the changed zone of this part, taken after this run.

rules.title: An STL made by code names its code
rules.statement: An STL that a script wrote names the script and its arguments, and says where each size comes from.
rules.why: Sleeves and shims written straight into the STL folder by a build script had no check at all.

attest.question: Which script and arguments made this STL, and is each size measured, from a fit ladder, or decided?
labels: made by the registered generator; every size is measured or from a fit ladder
made by the registered generator; at least one size is decided, never printed

rules.title: Read the rules of the feature before deciding
rules.statement: Before a part decision, read the rules of every feature the change touches (gate.py rules --category) and cite the rule id in the decision. A rule or a number changes only with the owner's word; the old value is kept as superseded in the same change and never comes back. Project numbers outrank the registry defaults.
rules.why: The rules existed and were not read: a session started from the part, not from the rulebook.

rules.title: Every number carries its evidence tag
rules.statement: Every number carries its tag: M measured on a real print, S simulated, U the owner's decision, D decided and not printed. Only a real print earns M, per material and nozzle, and its source names printer, nozzle and filament. A floor is not a design target: a dimensional rule has a target and a floor.
rules.why: A floor of 1.6 mm used as the design value passed a 2.5 mm wall, and the wall bulged.

rules.title: Rules in the plugin, numbers in one project file
rules.statement: General rules and their default numbers live in the plugin. A project vendors the tools with one command, holds only its parameters in one file that the rule text and the tools both read, and never edits a vendored check.
rules.why: A shared check was forked for one constant. A project number sat inside a shared tool. The version file of a vendored copy named a version it no longer was.
rules.note: Kept by gate/owner/params.json and gate/LOCK.json (intact, forked or stale).

rules.title: One command checks every part, and it stops the export
rules.statement: Before any export or print, one command runs every check over every printed part of every registered document, not only the part that was touched, and stops on any row without a waiver. A report is not a gate: the verdict is summed by the tool and carried by its exit code. Each result reads passed, failed or not run.
rules.why: Dozens of pockets with the same fault in nine parts were found only after one printed part had failed. Checks that were called gates printed a total that nothing read.
rules.note: This is gate.py run and gate.py export; the guard in the .3mf writer refuses a mesh without a stamp.

rules.title: Checks are run again after the last edit
rules.statement: Checks are run again after the last edit. A stamp belongs to one geometry: any later cut, fill or join ends it, and the part is checked again before it is exported.
rules.why: A relief cut deepened a lead-in and thinned the wall behind it. A later cut removed reliefs. Fills closed holes after the hole check had passed.
rules.note: Kept by the stamp: it is bound to the signature of the body.

rules.title: Parts are discovered, never typed into a check
rules.statement: Parts, bearings, pockets and plates are discovered from the documents and the projects, never typed into a list inside a check. One file names the documents, the STL folders and the projects; every check and the exporter read it.
rules.why: Five hand-kept part tables: a new part or bearing was invisible to every check until someone added a row.
rules.note: Kept by gate.py scan and gate/layout.json. A scan also names the parts with at most process.bought_hint_faces faces (a plain cylinder, a washer, a tube): a bought part that no name pattern of gate/project.json "not_printed" matches is listed as printed, and the owner adds a pattern or leaves it.

rules.title: A check measures the thing that fails
rules.statement: A check measures the thing that fails: a gap, not an overlap; material, not a face width; the swing of the tool, not a straight path; the slice, not the face angles; the target, not the floor. A new check is first run on a case that must fail. Every defect found in review or on the bench gets a check or a question that would catch it again. A print defect is traced from the model to the STL, the project mesh and the G-code.
rules.why: A plate with "0 mm3 of overlap" rubbed a turning part. A detector read a spigot as a melt relief and passed a part that had none.

rules.title: The verdict is a sum, and zero can be reached
rules.statement: A verdict is a count the tool sums over all its calls, never a printout read by eye. An intended hit is a waiver with its reason, so that zero open rows can be reached.
rules.why: One check had 72 intended hits on one part and no waiver file: its result was read as "nothing new in the changed zone".

rules.title: Limits, baselines and waivers are the owner's
rules.statement: A threshold, a baseline or a standard fix that an agent wrote is tagged D until the owner confirms it. A value looser than the registry default needs the tag M or U. A baseline is raised only by the owner. A waiver is the owner's, with the reason why the feature may stay; an order to export is not a reason.
rules.why: A standard fix, a gap limit, a pass line and four re-recorded baselines were written by the agent and read like decisions of the owner.
rules.note: Kept by gate.py params check and by the files under gate/owner.

rules.title: Records are keyed by the feature, not by a position
rules.statement: Baselines, waivers and answers are keyed by the feature or the part they belong to, never by a position in a list or a plate number. A key survives a small recut of its face and expires when the feature changes.
rules.why: A baseline keyed by plate number shifted by one when a plate left. Waivers keyed by coordinates were orphaned by a 0.5 mm cut.
rules.note: Kept by the feature anchor and the context hash.

rules.title: Old text does not stand beside the new rule
rules.statement: When a rule changes, the old value is marked superseded in the same change, everywhere it is written. Rule text in skills and project files is generated from the registry, not copied. An exception names the feature it is for and ends when that feature changes.
rules.why: An appendix still gave a pocket size two generations old; a plan said "no lead-in" a month after the lead-in had become the rule.

rules.title: A request about one part is solved in that part
rules.statement: A request about one part is solved inside that part. Cutting a printed neighbour is never proposed. An unprinted neighbour of the same design may move when the request allows it. A fit correction goes into the cheaper of two mating parts. What will change is restated in numbers before the geometry changes. A short question is answered, not acted on.
rules.why: A relief in a large printed base was offered to make room for a small plate. Three exports were reverted as misunderstood.
rules.note: "Change only the named part" and "neighbours of the same design can move" both stand; the condition is whether the neighbour is printed.

rules.title: Every side effect is reported
rules.statement: Every change that was not asked for but had to follow, and every new asymmetry, is reported with a simpler alternative. Designs and results are shown as drawings to scale.
rules.why: The owner found a relief groove and its ledge himself in the slicer.

rules.title: A printable part is complete in one pass
rules.statement: A part goes to the owner as printable only with its fasteners, inserts, reference bodies and export done in the same pass. Nothing floats. A concept says it is a concept and lists what is not designed yet.
rules.why: A concept tooth groove reached printed pulleys without a review.

rules.title: Several sessions, one model
rules.statement: Before a shared file or document is edited, check whether another session works on the same parts. STLs and the slicer project come from one version of the document. The project on disk corresponds to a commit. A shared interface changes only by agreement.
rules.why: Overlapping sessions produced an export set from mixed versions. A variant was synced into the project and never committed.

rules.title: A design with numbers is derived twice
rules.statement: A design with numbers that is not trivial is derived a second time, independently, before it is built. Every number of a generated specification is computed again.
rules.why: A generated specification left 0.04 mm to a belt.

rules.title: Every deviation is named and waits for a yes
rules.statement: Every deviation from a rule is named with its reason and waits for the owner's explicit yes. An open violation stays on the list until it is fixed or waived. Each decision records the document version and what was not verified.
rules.why: Open violations (2 mm under screw heads, a 0.95 mm wall, a sag five times its limit) stayed in a log for weeks with no waiver.
rules.note: Kept by the waivers and the triage list.

rules.title: Finish first, then ask; never guess a measurement
rules.statement: When the owner says to finish first, decide everything, record the open points and ask at the end. An ambiguous measurement is a question, not an assumption. Ask before trading printability for looks. Never start a print or save the owner's document unasked.
rules.why: No lost print is on record. Each line is a correction the owner made once.

rules.title: Done means the not-done list is empty or shown
rules.statement: A model change is finished when the STL is exported through the gate, the mesh is in the slicer project, the changed plates are sliced, the reference bodies and the build book are updated, and the report lists the parts to reprint, the printed parts that stop fitting, and what was not done. A pass that ends with a not-done list is not done: the list goes to the owner.
rules.why: Passes regularly ended with lists of what was not done: reference hardware at old positions, no screenshots, the book not regenerated.

rules.title: Search first; measure a replica with a caliper
rules.statement: Search for an existing model before modelling a common object, and report its licence. For a replica, measure with a caliper (a photo against a ruler is about 5 % off) and record each number with its source.
rules.why: The sizes of a bought board were read from a photo and its mount was printed wrong.
